comments.note: Edge case: if FixedDurationStrategy::isCacheFileValid() is called on a non-existent file, filemtime() returns false (cast to 0), making (time() - 0) always > any TTL duration, so the method returns false. This is safe behavior — no cache bypass — but the caller should guard against passing non-existent JSONFile instances upstream.

Edge case: files with a future mtime (e.g., clock skew or test fixtures) would make (time() - mtime) negative, which is less than durationInSeconds, so the file would be considered perpetually valid. Same behaviour exists in the AI cache equivalent; acceptable but worth documenting.

summary: All 3 files reviewed line-by-line: APICacheStrategyInterface, FixedDurationStrategy, ManualOnlyStrategy. Implementation is clean, minimal, and correct. All 5 acceptance criteria confirmed met. No blocking issues found. Three low-priority non-blocking observations recorded below.

comments.note: FixedDurationStrategy::isCacheFileValid() calls filemtime() which returns int|false. The false case (non-existent file) is used directly in arithmetic without an explicit check. Behaviour is safe (fails closed — returns false), but strict PHPStan levels will flag this. Once vendor is restored and PHPStan runs, if flagged the fix is: $mtime = filemtime($cacheFile->getPath()); if ($mtime === false) { return false; } ... The identical pattern exists in the AI cache reference, so PHPStan may already have a baseline entry for it.

FixedDurationStrategy::getID() returns the ID as a hardcoded string literal rather than a class constant. The AI cache equivalent uses STRATEGY_ID = 'fixed_duration' as a typed constant, enabling callers to reference FixedDurationStrategy::STRATEGY_ID without magic strings. Adding a public const string STRATEGY_ID = 'FixedDuration' and returning it from getID() would align the two systems and ease future strategy-switching logic.

Minor naming divergence from the AI cache reference: the AI cache uses DURATION_1_HOUR (underscore separator between digit and word) while the new API cache uses DURATION_1HOUR. The WP spec explicitly specified DURATION_1HOUR, so the implementation is fully compliant — this is a cross-system inconsistency to be aware of if the two DURATION constant sets are ever unified or extended.

No class-level or constructor docblock on FixedDurationStrategy or ManualOnlyStrategy. This matches the pattern in the AI cache reference strategy, so no change is required now — but adding minimal docblocks (especially a one-liner on the class and a @param on the constructor) would improve discoverability when these classes appear in IDE autocompletion.
